newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end mixed, pork bellies sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end mixed, pork bellies sharply higher.

text.p: CME lean hog futures closed mixed with a late rush of selling taking February lower, while deferred contracts closed sharply higher to up the 2.00-cent-per-lb limit.
Pork bellies closed sharply higher but concerns high prices will curb bacon consumption triggered light selling that pulled contracts off early limit gains.

USDA's U.S. Hogs and Pigs Report Friday continued to be the primary motivator for Tuesday's buying, particularly in deferred hog contracts and pork bellies. The report indicated there will be fewer hogs next year than analysts had expected.
However, ample hogs for current slaughter needs and steady to lower cash hog prices Tuesday at Midwest markets prompted the selling in February hogs.
"The cash news is not very good," said one trader. "They are calling cash (hogs) lower for Thursday."
Pork bellies were pulled off early limit gains by cash-connected selling. Talk circulated high cash belly prices slowed bacon usage.
"There is no bacon business," said one trader, who reported recent gains in cash belly prices have curbed retail sales.

Hogs closed down 0.275 to up 2.00 cents with February off 0.275 at 79.225 cents per lb. February hogs set a contract high early of 80.30 cents and April set a contract high of 76.675 cents. Pork bellies were up 2.250 to 1.575 cents with February up 1.925 at 82.350.
The markets will be closed Wednesday for the New Year's holiday.
